facts.statement: Gondwanatitan was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan (meaning "giant from Gondwana") was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan was a relatively small sauropod, reaching about 7 meters (23 ft) in length and weighing approximately 1 tonne.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan was a fairly small sauropod, only 7 meters (23 ft) long and weighing about 1 tonne (1.1 short tons).

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan possessed relatively gracile limb bones.
facts.quote: It had relatively gracile limb bones.

facts.statement: The middle caudal vertebrae of Gondwanatitan are distinctively heart-shaped, a feature that helps distinguish them from those of Aeolosaurus.
facts.quote: The middle caudal vertebrae are distinctively "heart-shaped", which allows isolated caudal vertebrae to be easily distinguished from those of Aeolosaurus.

facts.statement: The middle tail vertebrae of Gondwanatitan had elongated centra.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la parte media de su cola tenían centros alargados.

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan had vertebral lateral fossae that resembled shallow depressions.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan tenía fosas laterales vertebrales que se parecían a depresiones poco profundas.

facts.statement: The neural spines of the middle tail vertebrae are angled anteriorly when the vertebrae are aligned.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales de las vértebras de la cola media están inclinadas hacia delante cuando las vértebras están alineadas.

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan is distinguished by unique features including heart-shaped distal articular surfaces of proximal and middle caudal vertebrae, a developed and medially curved deltopectoral crest on the humerus, and a tibia with a dorsally projecting anterior proximal joint and a laterally curved cnemial crest.
facts.quote: Este taxón tiene las siguientes autapomorfías, superficies articulares distales de las vértebras caudales proximales y medias con forma de corazón, cresta deltopectoral del húmero desarrollada y curvada medialmente, la tibia con la parte anterior de la articulación proximal que proyecta dorsalmente y de la cresta cnemial curvada levemente a lateral.

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan lived in Brazil during the late Cretaceous Period, approximately 70 million years ago, when the region was part of the supercontinent Gondwana.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan was found in Brazil, at the time part of the southern supercontinent Gondwana, in the late Cretaceous Period (70 mya).

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan lived in South America during the late Cretaceous Period, approximately 83 million years ago in the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente 83 millones de años, en el Santoniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Gondwanatitan faustoi was discovered in 1983 on the farm of Yoshitoshi Myzobuchi in São Paulo, Brazil.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Gondwanatitan faustoi was discovered in 1983 on the farm of Yoshitoshi Myzobuchi in São Paulo, Brazil.

facts.statement: The type specimen was excavated between 1984 and 1986, with serious preparation work beginning in 1997.
facts.quote: The specimen was excavated between 1984 and 1986, but preparation work on the specimen did not begin in earnest until 1997.

facts.statement: Some elements of the holotype were lost in the National Museum of Brazil fire on September 2, 2018, though several elements survived and were recovered.
facts.quote: Some elements of the holotype were lost in the National Museum of Brazil fire on 2 September 2018, but several elements survived the fire and were recovered.

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan is a member of the clade Aeolosauridae.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan is a member of the clade Aeolosauridae.

facts.statement: Although its phylogenetic position is unclear, Gondwanatitan is not closely linked to members of Saltasaurinae and can be distinguished from more basal titanosaurians like Andesaurus and Malawisaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque su posición filogenética no está clara, este taxón no está estrechamente vinculado a los miembros de Saltasaurinae y se puede también distinguir de titanosaurianos más basales como Andesaurus y Malawisaurus.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus is considered the closest relative of Gondwanatitan.
It is debated whether Gondwanatitan is a valid genus; it was briefly considered a junior synonym of Aeolosaurus in 2001 but is now widely regarded as separate.
facts.quote: In 2001, G. faustoi was briefly transferred to the genus Aeolosaurus, making Gondwanatitan a junior synonym of that genus, but it has since been widely regarded as separate.

rejected.statement: Gondwanatitan was a tall herbivore that ate tough shoots and leaves from the tops of trees.
rejected.quote: Like some other sauropods, Gondwanatitan was tall and ate tough shoots and leaves from the tops of trees.

rejected.statement: The time range for Gondwanatitan is estimated from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species name G. faustoi is a patronym honoring Dr. Fausto L. de Souza Cunha, who led the excavation of the type specimen.
rejected.quote: The type and only named species, G. faustoi, is a patronym honoring Dr. Fausto L. de Souza Cunha, a former curator at the Museu Nacional/UFRJ who led the excavation of the type specimen.

rejected.quote: It was finally described as a new genus and species in 1999.
